claims.claim_ar: الأسلوب القرآني هنا يجمع بين الترغيب والترهيب كطريقة بلاغية لربط الجزاء بالإنذار والتحفيز.
claims.claim_en: The Qur'anic style here pairs exhortation (glad tidings) with warning (threat) as a rhetorical means of linking reward/promise with admonition to stimulate action.

claims.claim_ar: إدخال البشارة مرافقةً للإنذار هنا ليس مجرّد وصف بل لغايةٍ بلاغية: إرادة التنشيط وحثّ المكلفين على الاقتداء والعمل.
claims.claim_en: The pairing of glad tidings with warning is intentionally used as a rhetorical device to stimulate and motivate people to act (eradicative incentive).
claims.needs_review_reason: The tafsir statement is general about the Qur'anic method; confirm this specific function is being applied to this verse (2:236).

claims.source_quote_ar: قفاه ببشارة عباده الذين جمعوا بين التصديق والأعمال الصالحة
claims.claim_ar: الناقِل يشير إلى خاتمة الأمر بالترغيب بعد ذكر الترهيب؛ أي أن المقسوم يُقفل ببشارة للعباد الصالحين كحركة بلاغية في السياق.
claims.claim_en: The commentator notes a closure move: after mentioning threat/punishment the passage is closed with glad tidings for those believers who combined faith and righteous deeds — a rhetorical closure/contrastive movement in the discourse.
claims.needs_review_reason: The tafsir describes general discursive 'closure' following a warning; verify this reading is intended specifically for the placement/sequence in S2:236.

warnings: Source chunks supplied are tafsir excerpts discussing general rhetorical methods and some other verses; the explicit linkage of these tafsir observations to Q2:236 should be validated against direct commentary on this exact verse.
Many classical commentarial remarks are general (about the Qur'an's style) rather than verse-specific; claims extracted here reflect those general statements and so some claims are marked for review.
